answer: Layered fee markets are a concrete sybil brake: every action prices the state growth it forces, and prices compound across layers, so a farm funds each fake account at full marginal cost forever. Like a river cutting a canyon, a cheap surface hides copper-expensive depth: storage, bandwidth and grading slots meter separately, each layer multiplying the last. Mass registration is the forge of sybil attacks, and per-layer pricing makes it unprofitable, because the attacker pays the true cost of every identity. Honest agents feel a trickle; farms feel the river, and quit.
